name: Definite/Indefinite Articles
explanation: Danish holiday names can appear in either their indefinite (bare) form or their definite (-en/-et) form, depending on the expression. After prepositions like 'om', the definite form refers to an entire festive period (om julen — 'during Christmastime'). In many fixed expressions with 'til', the bare indefinite form is used instead, referring to the holiday as a named occasion (til påske — 'at Easter').

examples.danish: Vi rejser til Sverige om julen.
examples.english: We travel to Sweden during Christmastime.
We'll see each other at Easter.

name: Present tense (nutid)
explanation: Verbs describing traditions and celebrations — such as fejre (celebrate), pynte (decorate), and samles (gather) — conjugate regularly in the present tense by adding -r to the stem. This tense is used to describe what people habitually do during holidays and seasonal celebrations.

examples.danish: Vi fejrer jul med hele familien hver år.
examples.english: We celebrate Christmas with the whole family every year.

examples.danish: Familien pynter juletræet sammen om aftenen.
examples.english: The family decorates the Christmas tree together in the evening.
